title: Impact of Stock Split Announcements on Cumulative Abnormal Returns

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy  
Method: Event Study.  
We compare each firm’s realised return in a short window around its own stock–split announcement with an “expected” return generated by the market model (𝐸[𝑟𝑖𝑡]=αᵢ+βᵢ·𝑟ᵐ𝑡). Because the file already contains firm-specific β, we treat α≈0 over a very short horizon and compute abnormal return ARₜ = rₜ – β·rᵐₜ. Summing AR over the event window gives the cumulative abnormal return (CAR).

Key identifying assumptions  
1. No other value-relevant news for the same firms occurs within the event window (clean window).  
2. In the absence of the split announcement, expected abnormal returns are zero (market efficiency).  
3. β is stable between estimation and event windows.  

Under these assumptions, a non-zero average CAR can be causally attributed to the announcement.

## 2. R Code
```r
# ================================================================
# Impact of Stock-Split Announcements on Cumulative Abnormal Return
# ================================================================
library(readr)
library(dplyr)

# 1. Load data ----------------------------------------------------
df <- read_csv("experiments/exp_b/data/s55_data.csv",
               col_types = cols(
                 stock_id = col_integer(),
                 event_day = col_integer(),
                 ret = col_double(),
                 mkt_ret = col_double(),
                 beta = col_double()
               ))

# 2. Helper: function to compute CAR and its t-stat ---------------
get_car <- function(data, window_vec) {
  out <- data %>%
    filter(event_day %in% window_vec) %>%
    mutate(ar = ret - beta*mkt_ret) %>%
    group_by(stock_id) %>%
    summarise(CAR = sum(ar), .groups="drop")
  
  mean_car <- mean(out$CAR)
  se_car   <- sd(out$CAR)/sqrt(nrow(out))
  t_stat   <- mean_car / se_car
  list(mean = mean_car, se = se_car, t = t_stat, obs = nrow(out))
}

# 3. Main result: narrow window [-1,+1] ---------------------------
main_res <- get_car(df, -1:1)
cat("=== Main window [-1,+1] ===\n")
cat("Mean CAR   :", round(main_res$mean, 4), "\n")
cat("Std. Error :", round(main_res$se,   4), "\n")
cat("t-stat     :", round(main_res$t,    2), "\n")
cat("Firms      :", main_res$obs, "\n\n")

# 4. Robustness A: wider window [-5,+5] ---------------------------
robust1 <- get_car(df, -5:5)
cat("=== Robustness: window [-5,+5] ===\n")
cat("Mean CAR   :", round(robust1$mean, 4),
    " | t-stat :", round(robust1$t, 2), "\n\n")

# 5. Robustness B: placebo window [-10,-5] ------------------------
placebo <- get_car(df, -10:-5)
cat("=== Placebo: pre-event window [-10,-5] ===\n")
cat("Mean CAR   :", round(placebo$mean, 4),
    " | t-stat :", round(placebo$t, 2), "\n")
```

## 3. Expected Findings  
Prior literature shows that stock-split announcements are interpreted as good news about future cash flows or improved liquidity. I therefore expect:  
• Sign: Positive.  
• Magnitude: Roughly +1.5 % to +2.5 % average CAR in the tight [-1,+1] window, rising to about +3 %–4 % over [-5,+5].  
• The placebo window should yield a CAR statistically indistinguishable from zero, supporting the clean-window assumption.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: Compare CAR before and after the stock split announcement.
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: The announcement of a stock split is associated with a decrease in CAR.
